ranked_evidence.title: Allah - Wikipedia
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Allah. This article is about the Arabic word for God. For the Islamic conception of God, see God in Islam. Outside of Arabic languages, it is principally associated with Islam (in which it is also considered the proper name), although the term was used in pre-Islamic Arabia and continues to be used today by Arabic-speaking adherents of any of the Abrahamic religions, including Judaism and Christianity. The word "Allah" now conveys the superiority or sole existence of one God, but among the pre-Islamic Arabs, Allah was the supreme deity and worshipped alongside lesser deities in a pantheon "Pantheon (religion)"). The majority of scholars consider it to be derived from a contraction of the Arabic definite article *al-* and *ilāh* "deity, god" to *al-lāh* meaning "the deity, the God" as in the contraction of *al-ʾilāt* to *Allāt*. In Islamic usage and theology, *Allah* is God's most unique, proper name, and referred to as *Lafẓ al-Jalālah* ('the Word of Majesty').

Two Sahih Hadiths

Messenger of Allah (SAW) said:

‘O Jabir, the first thing Allah created before everything was the light (Noor) of your Prophet. That light moved wherever Allah willed, by His power. At that time, nothing else existed. There was no Tablet, no Pen, no Paradise, no Fire (Hell). There were no angels, no sky, no earth, no sun, no moon, no jinn, and no human.’”

(Ahmad, Musnad, IV-127; Hakim, Mustadrak, II-600/4175; Ibn Hibban, al-Ihsan, XIV-312/6404; al-Laknawi, al-Asaru’l-Merfua, p. 42-43; Qastalani, Mawahib al-Ladunniyya 1/6; Acluni, Kashfu’l-Khafa, 1/262-266)

It is also reported:

“When Allah wanted to create the creation, He divided this light into four parts.
From the first part He created the Pen.
From the second part He created the Tablet (Lawh al-Mahfuz).
From the third part He created the Throne.

Then He divided the fourth part again into four:
From the first part He created the carriers of the Throne.
From the second part He created the Kursi.
From the third part He created the other angels.

Then He divided the fourth part again into four:
From the first part He created the heavens.
From the second part He created the earths.
From the third part He created Paradise and Hell.

Then He divided the last part again into four:
From the first part He created the light of insight (the inner vision) of the believers.
From the second part He created the light of the hearts, which is knowing Allah.
From the third part He created the light of closeness, which is the light of Tawhid (La ilaha illa Allah Muhammadur Rasul Allah).”

The Messenger of Allah (sallallahu alayhi wa sallam) said in a hadith qudsi:

“Allah said: ‘I created you from My own light, and I created all other things from your light.’”

(Ahmad, Musnad IV-127; Hakim, Mustadrak II-600/4175; Ibn Hibban, al-Ihsan XIV-312/6404; Acluni, Kashfu’l-Khafa I-265/827)
